newsitem.title: USA: L.A. utility to sell power nationwide to churches.
newsitem.headline: L.A. utility to sell power nationwide to churches.

text.p: Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) will supply wholesale electricity to a marketing entity made up of "five of the largest African American religious denominations," the utility said Tuesday.

Details of the contract will be announced at a press conference on Wednesday, but the municipal utility said in a statement the move is part of plans to seek new revenue streams in preparation for deregulation of the power industry.
LADWP is the nation's largest municipal utility, but is loaded with debt and expected to face stiff competition from other suppliers once California begins to open its electricity market next year.

Revelation Corp of America has formed a power marketing subsidiary, Revelation Energy Resources Inc, so that it can sell power along with other services to African American churches nationwide, an LADWP spokeswoman explained.
Information on the amount of power LADWP will be supplying to the power marketer and the length of the contract were not immediately available.
Earlier this month, LADWP announced plans to form a strategic alliance with Duke-Louis Dreyfus, a joint venture of North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp.
The partnership, which is still awaiting final approval by the Los Angeles city council, is aimed at improving the utility's chances of retaining customers and raising wholesale trading revenues.
